title: Exit code change for Incomplete verdict (from 2 to 3) and command errors (from 2 to 1) breaks automation compatibility
body: The five-tier exit code scheme (0=approve, 1=command error, 2=degraded approve, 3=incomplete, 10=reject) repurposed exit code 2 from its historical meaning of 'partial/incomplete' to 'degraded approve'. This silently shifts every code path that previously returned 2 for Incomplete (e.g., `partial_report`, `run_job` timeout/failure, `resolve_result` for non-terminal jobs) to exit 3, and every code path that returned 2 for command failures (e.g., bad args, bad config) to exit 1. Any CI/deployment script that checked for exit code 2 as 'not fully approved' will now see either 1 (error) or 3 (incomplete) and may misinterpret the result — most dangerously, treating exit 0 as the only failure case and proceeding with a degraded-approve report. The provided spec docs (SKILL.md, ship.md) do not define the exit codes, so this is not a spec violation, but the change is user-visible and breaks existing contracts without migration guidance. Affected call sites: `main.rs` lines using `std::process::exit(2)` changed to `exit(1)` (e.g., args parsing errors, job not found, bad config) and `cli/tail.rs` `exit_code(Verdict::Incomplete, _)` returning 3 instead of 2. `partial_report` (cli/mod.rs) and all three `run_job` outcome branches use the new 3. `resolve_result` in main.rs returns 1 for non-terminal jobs instead of 2.
recommendation: Document the exit codes in the `--help` output and in ship.md/SKILL.md. Consider adding a transition period where Incomplete still returns 2 if no explicit `--exit-format` is provided, or add a `--exit-codes` flag to opt into the new scheme. At minimum, ensure the changelog highlights the mapping change.

title: `resolve show` output appends human-readable history lines to pretty-printed JSON, breaking machine consumption
body:
The `resolve show` command (used by ship.md for cross-round state reconstruction) outputs a JSON block via `serde_json::to_string_pretty` and then appends `
history:
  (round)  reason...` as raw text lines. The resulting output is not valid JSON and cannot be parsed by jq or similar tools. The symmetrical `dismiss show` command outputs pure valid JSON (no appended lines), creating an inconsistency. Scripts that automate `resolve show <id>` to retrieve card details will misparse or fail. The ship.md protocol references `resolve show <id>` as a cross-round state reconstruction read, but does not specify whether the output must be machine-readable JSON or human-readable text — the current hybrid form satisfies neither.
recommendation: Either output pure JSON (including history as a JSON array field inside the card object) and let the client format it for display, or add a `--format` flag to `resolve show` to select between text/human and JSON output. Align with `dismiss show` behavior: prefer a unified `--format json|table` interface.

title: Fuzzy carry matching can silently erase a distinct new finding
quote:
c.id == n.id
                || (c.origin == Origin::Carried && crate::consolidate::dedup::is_same_bug(c, &n))
body: The new fallback treats any overlapping finding with a sufficiently similar title or quote as the same bug as a carried finding, even when their stable IDs differ. Two distinct defects can legitimately share a line range and a generic title such as "missing validation". In that case the new finding is discarded; only its model name is merged, while its ID, body, severity, confidence, recommendation, and `Origin::New` are lost. This is especially dangerous when the carried ID is dismissed: the merged result is subsequently marked dismissed under the old ID, so a genuinely new blocking defect can be exempted and the review can incorrectly approve. `stats.new` also no longer records it. Preserve ambiguous new findings instead of collapsing them based on this heuristic.
recommendation: Use exact ID matching for destructive carry absorption. If quote drift must be reconciled, retain both findings or emit an explicit ambiguous/re-anchored relationship for later adjudication; do not discard the new finding or inherit the carried finding's dismissal state unless identity is established deterministically.

title: Worker spawn failure leaves an unreapable Pending job
body: The background path creates the job before spawning the detached worker, but the spawn-error branch exits without updating that job. The resulting state is Pending with no PID. `reap_if_dead` explicitly leaves Pending jobs without a PID untouched because it cannot determine liveness, so this record remains Pending indefinitely and can be mistaken for work that may still start. Repeated dispatch failures accumulate permanent zombie jobs.
recommendation: On spawn failure, use the already-open `JobStore` to transition the created job to `Failed`, recording the spawn error and exit code 1, before returning. If that terminal write also fails, surface both errors. Alternatively, make job creation and successful worker registration transactional through a launch state that can be deterministically reaped.

title: Guard-write errors still leave background jobs non-terminal and externally report the wrong outcome
body: Returning `1` only changes the detached worker's process exit code; it does not persist a terminal job state. In production this worker was spawned with stderr redirected to null, and the parent neither waits for nor observes its exit code. Therefore a transient `update_if_active` failure can still leave the database row Pending. `result` does not invoke `reap_if_dead`, so clients that poll only `redteam result` can continue seeing “not done” indefinitely. If `status` is eventually called, lazy reaping changes the job to Failed with exit code 2, losing the intended exit code 1 and the actual database error. Thus the delta does not resolve the user-visible hanging/diagnostic failure it describes.
recommendation: Do not rely on the detached worker's unobserved return code. Establish a parent/worker startup handshake or supervision channel so failure to enter Running is persisted by a process with an independent store connection. At minimum, retry a guarded transition to Failed with the original error and exit code 1, and make all job-observation paths, including `result`, reap dead Pending/Running workers. Preserve the original startup error when reaping rather than replacing it with the generic exit code 2.

title: 模型控制的 needs 路径可实现项目内任意文件读取，导致信息泄露
quote:
fn need_section(ex: &crate::tools::ToolExecutor, need: &crate::domain::NeedEntry) -> Option<String> {
    let text = ex.read_capped(&need.path)?;
body: 二阶段补查机制（second_pass_prompt, need_section）允许模型在 needs 数组中指定任意相对路径。ToolExecutor::read_capped 通过 safe_join + canonicalize + starts_with 进行安全检查，限制在 canonical_root 内。但是，该检查只要求路径在项目根目录内部，并不限制必须是变更集内的文件。因此模型可以指示读取项目根下任意文件（如 .env, 密钥文件, 数据库配置, 其他敏感源码），其内容会进入 prompt 的补查证据段，并最终出现在评审报告（finding 的 quote 或 evidence）中。尽管有 NEED_SECTION_BYTE_CAP（64KB）和 DOC_EVIDENCE_TOTAL_CAP（256KB）的字节帽，但敏感内容仍可能被截断输出。该攻击面在 adversarial review 中尤为严重：攻击者可以构造一个 PR，其模型输出 malicious needs 来泄露项目敏感信息。
recommendation: 在 second_pass_prompt 和 need_section 中添加额外检查：need.path 必须属于变更集内的文件（即在 bundles 的某 Bundle::files 中出现过），禁止读取变更集外的任何文件。对于 doc 模式，限制为 targets 和 spec_docs 中指定的文件。移除从项目根目录任意路径读取的能力。或者在读取后但加入 prompt 前，对敏感文件模式（如 .env, *secret*, *key*）进行过滤/红action。

title: lens 字段从 output_contract 和 Finding 结构体中移除，丧失 finding 到攻击面规则的追溯能力
quote:
pub struct Finding {
    pub id: String,
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub title: String,
—  pub lenses: Vec<String>,
body: 本次变更移除了 RawFinding.lens 字段、Finding.lenses 字段、RunMeta.lenses 字段，以及整个 lens/mod.rs 模块。output_contract 模板中不再要求模型输出 lens 标签。虽然攻击面规则仍以固有文本形式嵌入模板，但模型输出时不再需要指定 finding 属于哪个规则，系统也无法从结果中判断每条 finding 对应 L1-L5/D1-D5 中的哪个规则。这降低了评审结果的可解释性，无法后处理聚合特定规则的安全分析报告。旧模型输出中带有的 lens 字段会被 serde 静默忽略，但不转化到 Finding 中。
recommendation: 恢复 lens 字段（至少作为可选字段），并在 output_contract 中保留 'lens: the id of the rule' 要求。如果希望保持简洁，可以在系统内部通过 auto-classification（基于规则文本蕴含）推断，但目前没有该机制。最简单的修复是在 Finding 中添加 Optional<String> 字段用于规则归属，不影响去 lens 化的主要设计方向。

quote:
c.id == n.id
                || (c.origin == Origin::Carried && crate::consolidate::dedup::is_same_bug(c, &n))
body: The new fallback treats any overlapping finding with a sufficiently similar title or quote as the same bug as a carried finding, even when their stable IDs differ. title: Scope/base validation only at CLI layer – library functions silently ignore --base
body: The fix for the 'clean tree silent approve' incident adds scope validation only in `main.rs` (lines 392–400). The underlying library functions `run_review_dispatch` (line 483), `run_code_review` (line 394), and `run_review` (line 297) accept a pre-resolved `ReviewArgs.scope` without any cross-validation against `base`. Any code path that constructs `ReviewArgs` programmatically (e.g., API callers, future automation, or third-party tooling) will reproduce the exact original bug: `--base main` with `scope: "working-tree"` silently ignores the base and reviews only the working tree, producing an empty diff → 0 findings → silent approve. The version-skew case is especially dangerous: old `args.json` files written before this fix contain `scope: "working-tree"` with `base: "main"`; the new worker reads and honors them uncritically, preserving the broken behavior for queued jobs.
recommendation: Move the scope resolution logic (the match on scope/base) into a shared function called from both `main.rs` and `run_review_dispatch`, and have `run_review_dispatch` re-resolve (or at least validate) the scope before use. For the version-skew path, upgrade read: after deserializing args.json, if `scope == "working-tree"` and `base.is_some()`, either error out or force `scope = "branch"` with a warning.

title: on_meta stamps models/lenses into state before fan-out completes, causing state/report inconsistency on assemble_report failure
quote:
if let Some(s) = sink { s.on_meta(&model_names, &lens_ids); }
    let raw = run_doc_fanout(provider, &input, &lenses, &focus, &oopts, sink).await;
body: In both `run_review` (line 356) and `run_code_review` (line 440), `s.on_meta(&model_names, &lens_ids)` is called before the fan-out executes. If the subsequent `assemble_report` call fails (e.g., anchor/dedup/verify panics or returns an error), the job state file (written by `on_meta`) already contains non-empty `models` and `lenses` arrays, but the partial report constructed in `run_job`'s `Done(Err)` path calls `partial_report`, which produces a report with empty `models`/`lenses` (line 595–597). A user running `redteam status` sees resolved models/lenses, but `redteam result` shows empty arrays – a confusing inconsistency. While this scenario requires an abnormal `assemble_report` failure, the mismatch undermines trust in the observability layer.
recommendation: Option A: defer `on_meta` to just before `assemble_report` (after fan-out succeeds). Option B: make `partial_report` read the latest state file's models/lenses instead of hardcoding empty arrays, so the partial report reflects what was actually resolved even on failure.

title: `partial_report` returns empty models/lenses despite `on_meta` having stamped them into state — partial-failure result JSON loses metadata
quote:
run: RunMeta {
            job_id: job_id.to_string(),
            models: vec![],
            model_ids: vec![],
            lenses: vec![],
body:
The `on_meta` callback (lines 21-23 of the diff) is designed to stamp models and lenses into the job state early, during the "running" phase, so they are visible before the job completes.  `JobCellSink::on_meta` (cli.rs:560-567) writes `st.models` and `st.lenses` to the state file.  The callers in `run_review` and `run_code_review` (cli.rs:356, 440) invoke `on_meta` synchronously *before* the fan-out.

However, the partial-failure path (`partial_report`, cli.rs:573-608) does **not** read the job state to recover these fields.  It hard-codes `models: vec![]`, `model_ids: vec![]`, `lenses: vec![]` (cli.rs:595-597).  The state file at that point *does* contain the models and lenses written by `on_meta* (the callers in `run_job` re-read `st` from state before calling `write_partial_result`), but the JSON result emitted for a timed-out or failed job carries empty arrays.

This creates a silent data loss: a user or dashboard reading the partial result JSON sees no models or lenses, even though the data was explicitly written to state and could have been propagated.  The inconsistency is directly introduced by this diff: before `on_meta` existed, neither the state file nor the partial report had models/lenses, so the two were consistent (both empty).  Now the state file is populated but the report is not — a regression in observability.

**Concrete impact**:
- A user inspecting a partial (timeout/failure) result sees `"models":[]`, `"lenses":[]` and cannot tell which models or lenses were being used when the job failed.
- The RunMeta in the partial result is an incomplete truth, undermining the "running 期 status 可见" design intent stated in the trait doc.

**Fix**: In `partial_report`, read the job state with `crate::state::job::read_state(ws, job_id)` and populate `report.run.models`, `report.run.model_ids`, `report.run.lenses` from `st.models` and `st.lenses` (with model_ids resolved from cfg, or left as fallback).  The state is guaranteed to exist at this point because `on_meta` runs before any fan-out, so even a pre-fan-out crash would not reach `partial_report`.
recommendation: Read the job state inside partial_report and set report.run.models = st.models (the model names), report.run.lenses = st.lenses. For model_ids, either resolve from the config or accept the gap as lower priority — the model names alone are already valuable for a partial report. The state is guaranteed present because on_meta runs before fan-out, and partial_report is only reached after fan-out (either via timeout or error).

title: Empty bundles manifest breaks resume contract
body: When `bundles.is_empty()` in `run_code_review`, the code still calls `run_code_fanout()`, which writes an empty manifest (0 cells) to the job store. The job completes normally with `JobStatus::Done` and a warning. However, `run_resume` treats an empty manifest as a crash-before-fan-out signal and returns `Incomplete` with the message "resume: empty manifest (job crashed before fan-out); nothing to resume". This contradicts the actual job state (Done, completed normally) and confuses any downstream consumer that attempts resume on an otherwise successful zero-bundle job. The check for 0 bundles must happen before `run_code_fanout` is called so that either the manifest never gets written (if the job check is fast) or the manifest contains at least a sentinel cell.

title: Scope validation accepts --scope branch without --base, then fails with confusing error
body: In `main.rs` lines 392-400, the new scope inference logic only rejects the combination `--scope working-tree` + `--base`. If the user passes `--scope branch` without `--base`, it passes through (pattern `(Some(s), _)`), reaching `build_registry` → `run_review_dispatch` → `changed_files` which eventually bails at `collect_code` with "branch scope requires --base". This is a UX regression: the user explicitly requested branch scope, the parser accepted it, and the error manifests deep in the call stack without mentioning the `--scope` flag. The old code would have silently defaulted `scope` to `"working-tree"` even when `--scope branch` was passed (ignoring the user's explicit intent), so this is strictly less confusing than before, but it is still confusing. Additionally, if `bundles` happens to be empty (e.g., no reviewable files), the empty-bundles guard at cli.rs line 444 would render the confusing label "branch ?...HEAD" in its warning.

title: Unicode confusables bypass verdict prefix detection, flipping Upheld→Refuted
body: `classify_refute` performs ASCII-only `starts_with` checks on the lowercased title (lines 71, 75).  A model output that uses Unicode homoglyphs/confusables in place of ASCII letters — e.g. Greek `υ` (U+03C5) for `u`, Cyrillic `е` (U+0435) for `e` — will not match `"upheld"` and will fall through to the else branch on line 77.  The else branch unconditionally classifies the finding as `Refuted` with a contract-drift warning.  This means a model that intends to say "upheld" — or accidentally produces a typographic variant — gets its output inverted: the original (correct) finding is treated as refuted, suppressing a real defect.  The same class affects the `"refuted"` check on line 71 (safe fallback but adds noise).  Because the fix requires checking only the first finding's title with a single canonicalization point, adding more prefix patterns (e.g. `"upheld"`, `"claim upheld"`) does not close the class — every new variant a model emits becomes another entry in an arms-race allowlist.
recommendation: Replace the per-prefix ASCII starts_with checks with a single Unicode-aware canonicalization function that: (a) decomposes confusables (NFKC normalization), (b) strips known verdict-prefix patterns in normalized space, (c) falls back to the empty-array contract (Upheld) for truly non-matching output.  Do not add another prefix arm — that leaves the class open.

title: Only first finding's title determines verdict; subsequent findings silently ignored
body: `classify_refute` examines only `findings.first()` (line 66).  All remaining elements of the model's response are ignored for verdict determination.  The refute prompt contracts (both code and doc templates) instruct the model to return EXACTLY ONE finding when refuted and an empty array when upheld, but models routinely violate output contracts in practice (as the code's own comment on line 62 acknowledges: "守約模型想表達 upheld 也會輸出 finding").  If a model returns multiple findings — e.g. finding[0] with title `"Claim upheld: appears safe"` and finding[1] with title `"REFUTED: guard exists at L10"` — the function returns `Upheld`, silently discarding the genuine refutation.  The old heuristic (`!call.findings.is_empty()` → Refuted) was strictly more robust against multi-finding contract violations.  This is a regression that reintroduces the precise class of false negatives the original design sought to eliminate (dogfood r1 12bbeb4c).
recommendation: Change `classify_refute` to inspect ALL findings, not just the first.  If ANY finding has a refuted-type title the verdict is Refuted.  Alternatively, restore the old invariant: non-empty → Refuted falls back only when no finding carries a recognized verdict-prefix.  Document why only the first finding is read if that is the intentional design, and add a test that multi-finding responses do not drop refutations.

title: partial_report produces empty models/lenses despite job state having them via on_meta
quote:
models: vec![],
            model_ids: vec![],
            lenses: vec![],
body: The new `on_meta` method writes models and lenses into the job state (via `JobCellSink::on_meta`) before fan-out. However, the `partial_report` function (used for failure/timeout paths) hardcodes `models: vec![]` and `lenses: vec![]` in the constructed `RunMeta`, ignoring the values now available in the job state. When `run_job` encounters a timeout or error, it calls `partial_report` and then `write_partial_result`, which preserves the state's models/lenses but embeds the empty arrays in the partial report. A user retrieving the result via `redteam result <job_id>` sees a report with empty `run.models` and `run.lenses`, while `redteam status <job_id>` correctly shows them. This inconsistency did not exist before because the job state had no models/lenses fields; the change activates a dormant inconsistency in the partial-report path.
recommendation: Update `partial_report` to read `models` and `lenses` from the job state (via `read_state`) when available, falling back to empty arrays. Alternatively, propagate `model_names` and `lens_ids` as parameters to `partial_report` from the `run_job` error/timeout handlers.

title: Silent write failure in JobCellSink::on_meta hides missing models/lenses from status
body: JobCellSink::on_meta writes models and lenses into the job state, but discards any I/O error from write_state (line 565: `let _ = crate::state::job::write_state(...)`). If writing fails (disk full, permissions, DB corruption), the job state silently retains empty models/lenses vectors. A user polling job status would see empty models/lenses even though the review is running with specific models and lenses — undermining the feature's purpose and eroding trust in the displayed metadata. All other write-heavy methods in JobCellSink (manifest, on_cell, on_phase) follow the same discard pattern, so this is a design-wide weakness now extended to user-visible metadata.
recommendation: At minimum log the error, e.g. `if let Err(e) = crate::state::job::write_state(...) { log::error!("failed to write models/lenses to job state: {e}"); }`. For higher resilience, consider returning a fallible result from `on_meta` so callers can decide to abort or warn, but that would require changing the trait signature — logging is the pragmatic first step.

title: 验收成功标准未量化，无法判定批 1 是否通过
quote: 前置进批 1 验收的最低配：异语料 smoke（中型 Rust 仓真 PR 一跑）。翻转后的回归监控项：①多模型复验…
body: §4 验证部分称“批 1 验收最低配：异语料 smoke 一跑”。但“smoke”未定义通过条件：是否所有 finding 都需合理？人工评判的 inter‑rater 标准？是否接受 false positive/negative 比例？也提到“翻转后的回归监控项”，但监控阈值未定义（例如“needs 触发率”多少算异常？）。由于批 1 直接翻默认，如果没有可复现、可客观度量的成败标准，团队无法确认翻转是否安全，也无法在后续迭代中评估回归。
recommendation: 为每个验收项写明确量指标：例如 smoke 需在至少某规模 PR 上运行且 findings 空误报率 ≤5%；回归监控项需设定健康基线（如 needs 触发率 <1%，降级路径覆盖率>80%）并记录初始值。

title: Each store.rs operation opens a new ProjDb connection, re-executing DDL and pragma every time
body: Every public function in store.rs (write_manifest, read_manifest, append_partial, read_partial, write_args_raw, read_args_raw, write_result, read_result, write_result_md, read_result_md) calls the local `db(ws)` helper (store.rs:37-39), which calls ProjDb::open, which creates a new SQLite Connection, sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, and executes the entire `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` batch (5 tables, ~40 lines of DDL). With the fanout pattern in orchestrate/mod.rs, a single review can trigger dozens of `append_partial` calls (one per cell) and one `write_manifest` call — each opening a fresh connection and re-executing all DDL. This is not just wasteful: the `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` setting is a per-connection setting that is only advisory — if another connection opened the database without WAL (e.g., a third-party tool), the new connection re-asserts it, but the transient window without WAL could cause different connections to see different journal modes. Furthermore, creating 20+ SQLite connections per review run adds measurable overhead (each connection allocates internal buffers, opens file descriptors, and checks the database integrity).
recommendation: Cache the ProjDb connection, e.g., store it in a thread_local or pass it as a parameter rather than calling `db(ws)` on every operation. Since all operations target the same project database, one connection per process (with the JobCellSink mutex coordinating writes) is sufficient and avoids repeated DDL execution.

title: `--dismissed` pass-through creates split-brain ledger: dismissal writes go to proj.db but review reads from user-provided db
quote: 用户显式传 `--dismissed`/`--no-dismissed` 时原样透传（那是合法的覆盖语义）。
body:
The spec (line 19) declares that user `--dismissed`/`--no-dismissed` is passed through as "legitimate override semantics." However, the `redteam dismiss add` subcommand (main.rs:670) always opens `.redteam/proj.db` via `ProjDb::open(&cwd)` — it has no mechanism to target a user-provided db path. Meanwhile, `load_ledger` (cli.rs:78-92) reads from the user-provided `--dismissed` path when one is given. This creates a structural split:

1. Ship agent writes dismissal cards to `.redteam/proj.db` (`dismiss add` at main.rs:670).
2. If user passed `--dismissed custom.db`, the *review* tool loads from `custom.db` and is blind to cards in `.redteam/proj.db`.
3. The escalation brake chain (`dismiss show <id>`, ship.md lines 99-104) also reads from `.redteam/proj.db` (the default), not the custom db.
4. The `--no-dismissed` path is even more severe: the review runs with zero exemptions, so `previously_dismissed` is never set on any finding, the brake chain never triggers, and human-confirmed findings are silently re-adjudicated from scratch.

The protocol claims this is "legitimate override" but the underlying tooling has no cross-db awareness. Dismissals the agent records are invisible to subsequent review rounds whenever a custom `--dismissed` flag is active, and the escalation brake becomes inert under `--no-dismissed`.

Fix: ship must intercept `--dismissed`/`--no-dismissed` and either (a) reject them with a clear explanation that they break the escalation protocol, or (b) make *all* dismissal commands (`dismiss add`, `dismiss set-status`, `dismiss show`) accept an optional `--db` parameter so the agent can target the same database the review tool is using. The pass-through-as-is approach is incomplete — it only handles the read side but not the write side.
recommendation: Intercept `--dismissed`/`--no-dismissed` from user args and reject them with a protocol-level error message, or add a `--db` parameter to all `dismiss` subcommands and make the agent pass the user-provided path through to every dismissal operation it performs. The current 'pass-through + always-write-to-proj.db' design is a cross-db inconsistency that silently breaks the escalation brake chain.

title: cancel 的状态终态写用 `let _ =` 静默吞错，与 worker 收尾竞态可丢失取消
body: Cmd::Cancel 读到 Running job 后先 `libc::kill(pid, SIGTERM)`，再 `let _ = write_state(&ws, &s)` 落 Cancelled，然后无条件 `println!("cancelled")` 并返回 0。两个问题叠加成数据/状态一致性缺陷：(1) 若 write_state 因 SQLITE_BUSY（worker 正在写 progress）失败，Cancelled 状态没有落库，但用户已看到 “cancelled”，命令退出 0，实际 job 未被标记取消。(2) run_job 收尾（cli.rs:824-833）以 `read_state` 读到的最新状态为底稿判断 `cancelled = matches!(latest.status, Cancelled)`，若 cancel 的写在 worker 收尾读之后才（成功）落库，或根本没落库，worker 会把 status 覆盖为 Done。取消与收尾之间没有任何跨进程互斥或 CAS，取消在竞态窗口内可被静默丢失。
recommendation: cancel 写状态失败时不应打印成功；检查 write_state 返回值，失败则报错并返回非零。取消应通过 CAS/条件更新（如 `UPDATE jobs SET state=... WHERE 当前 status IN (running,pending)`）实现原子化，或在 worker 收尾对 Cancelled 做不可逆终态保护，避免收尾覆盖已取消状态。

title: Markdown table broken by pipe character in human_tokens output
body: The `human_tokens` function (line 14-21) returns strings containing a bare pipe character `|` when tokens ≥ 1000, e.g. `` `2620877` | `2.62M` ``. This output is placed directly into a Markdown table cell at lines 86-87 via `format!("  | Input Tokens  | {} |\n", ...)`. Markdown parsers interpret the bare `|` as a column separator, creating an extra column that breaks the table structure and makes the Info table unreadable. The test at line 201 asserts the broken string is present, confirming the bug is intentional in the code but not recognized as a rendering defect.
recommendation: Remove the pipe separator from `human_tokens`. Show only the abbreviated form (e.g. `` `2.62M` ``) when tokens exceed 1000, or place the raw token count on a separate line or in parentheses without a pipe. For example: `if n >= 1_000_000 { format!("`{:.2}M`", n as f64 / 1_000_000.0) }`. There is no valid way to include a bare `|` inside a Markdown table cell.

title: Empty-bundles warning untested — regression would go undetected
body: The new empty-bundles guard (lines 443–446) pushes a warning into `raw.warnings` when `bundles.is_empty()`.  The existing `code_review_empty_changes_approves` test (line 1423) calls `run_code_review` with an empty `changes` vector, which triggers this branch, but the test only asserts `report.findings.is_empty()` and `code == 0`.  It never inspects `report.run.warnings`, so a regression that drops the warning, changes its message, or breaks the condition would pass silently.  The comment on lines 442–443 explicitly cites a prior production incident (r1 20260703 clean-tree false-green), making this a material observability regression gap.
recommendation: Add an assertion such as `assert!(report.run.warnings.iter().any(|w| w.contains("no reviewable evidence")), "empty-changes warning missing")` to the existing test, or add a dedicated test case that verifies the warning content and presence.

title: Refute classifier treats natural-language prefix variants as machine verdicts
body: The refute prompt defines a strict machine signal: a refutation title must use the exact `"REFUTED: "` prefix, and upheld claims must be represented only by an empty findings array. The classifier instead accepts any title whose lowercased text starts with `refuted`, without requiring the canonical delimiter or isolating a verdict field. That lets non-canonical natural-language variants such as `Refuted? No, the claim holds`, `refutedness is not established`, `REFUTED — actually not`, and equivalents be silently classified as `Refuted`, which suppresses the original finding from blocking. This is an input-parsing boundary issue: the dimension being bypassed is prefix-boundary/canonical-token ambiguity, not just one missed string.
recommendation: Normalize refute output through a single canonical parser that accepts only the exact contract token, e.g. `REFUTED: ` followed by a non-empty reason, or better a dedicated verdict field/enumeration. Treat any non-canonical non-empty output as contract drift requiring conservative handling rather than adding more prefix cases; per-case allow/deny-list patches leave the prefix-ambiguity class open.

title: Silent error discard in `JobCellSink::on_meta` may leave job state with empty models/lenses during running phase
body: The `on_meta` implementation in `JobCellSink` (cli.rs:560-567) silently discards the result of `write_state`. If the write fails (e.g. database I/O error, lock contention), the job state’s `models` and `lenses` remain empty for the duration of the running phase, despite the design intent to make them visible in `status` during `running`. While this error-handling pattern is consistent with the other `CellSink` methods (`manifest`, `on_cell`, `on_phase`), it is a systemic robustness weakness. A status-polling consumer (e.g. a dashboard or CLI `job status` command) would see blank `models`/`lenses` fields even though the job has successfully resolved them, undermining the observability goal this commit introduces. The issue is exacerbated because the same silent discard exists in the other `CellSink` methods, so fixing only `on_meta` would leave the class open.
recommendation: Propagate the error or at minimum log a warning when `write_state` fails inside `on_meta`. For resilience, consider writing models/lenses in `manifest` instead (which already has a write path) or adding a retry with backoff. A centralized write helper that logs failures would address all `CellSink` methods at once rather than patching per-method.

title: SSE-vs-JSON body routing by substring `contains("data:")` misclassifies whole-JSON responses as unparseable streams → non-retryable `Parse` burns the cell
quote: if !sse.contains("data:") {
body: `AnthropicBackend::turn` decides "is this SSE?" with `sse.contains("data:")`, and `parse_anthropic_stream` repeats the identical check. The input-space dimension being bypassed is body-format detection: any complete JSON body (success or gateway error) that merely contains the substring `data:` anywhere is routed to the SSE line parser, where no line begins with `data:`, `saw_event` stays false, the function returns `None`, and `turn` maps that to `ProviderError::Parse("anthropic stream missing content")` — non-retryable, so `retry_classified` is bypassed and the cell is burned. This is exactly the D1 failure mode ("误判为 Parse 会绕过重试") that this same change is trying to defend against. Representative variants and equivalents of the class: (1) a successful non-stream JSON response whose model text contains `data:` — in this code-review domain that is ordinary content (YAML `data:` keys, Rust named-field `data:` initializers, quoted code in findings bodies); (2) a 200-wrapped error body whose message references a `data:` path (e.g. a schema violation at `properties.data`), which also silently defeats `error_body_to_provider_error` classification; (3) JSON with leading whitespace/BOM (detection unaffected by trimming of the whole body); (4) the mirror instance already live in `OpenAiBackend::post` / `parse_openai_stream`, which uses the same `!sse.contains("data:")` guard — and the OpenAI path is the one all three current providers use, so the class is not hypothetical; (5) SSE-spec multi-line `data:` fields (data split across lines must be joined before JSON parsing) are dropped line-by-line here and can likewise starve `saw_event` into a false `Parse`. Per-case patches (e.g. also testing for `"event:"`) leave the class open.
recommendation: Establish a single canonicalization point for body-format routing: trim the body and first attempt `serde_json::from_str` on the WHOLE body (an SSE body of `event:`/`data:` lines can never parse as one JSON value, so the decision is unambiguous); only if that fails, parse as an event stream by scanning for line-initial `data:` prefixes — never substring containment. Route both the Anthropic and the OpenAI backend through this one helper (natural extension of `parse_envelope_json`'s role) so D1 error classification sees every whole-JSON body regardless of its text content. Adding more substring cases leaves the class open; only the parse-first canonical order closes it.

title: Truncated mid-generation streams are accepted as complete turns: no `message_stop`/completeness gate, and partial tool JSON silently becomes `{}`
quote: if !saw_event {
body: `parse_anthropic_stream` accepts any body in which at least one `data:` line parsed (`saw_event`). If the stream is truncated cleanly (proxy closes early, gateway gives up mid-generation — precisely the degradation this change is built to survive), `resp.text()` still succeeds, the final half-written event fails `serde_json::from_str` and is silently skipped (`Err(_) => continue`), `message_stop`/`finish_reason` never arrive, and the function returns `Some(AssistantTurn)` with silently truncated `text`. Two concrete losses: (1) truncated findings JSON reaches `parse_lens_output` and fails → one wasted REPAIR round (extra tokens/latency) instead of consuming the available retry budget via a retryable `Unavailable`; (2) a `tool_use` block whose accumulated `input_json_delta` was cut mid-JSON fails `serde_json::from_str(&args)` and is silently replaced by `json!({})` — the tool then executes with empty arguments (e.g. `read_files` with `paths: []`) and the loop continues on garbage rather than surfacing the failure. Nothing in the returned turn distinguishes "complete stream" from "cut stream" (`finish_reason: None` is the only residue, and nothing acts on it here).
recommendation: Gate completeness: if no `message_stop` event was seen (equivalently, no terminal `stop_reason` arrived via `message_delta`), return an error classified as `Unavailable` (retryable) instead of a partial turn. Additionally, when accumulated `partial_json` fails to parse, surface it (Parse/Unavailable with the accumulated prefix in the message) rather than `unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({}))`, so a truncated tool call cannot execute with silently emptied arguments.

title: Empty code evidence is still reported as a clean approve with exit code 0
body: The new empty-diff handling only appends a warning after fanout. The report then continues through assemble_report, where an empty finding set computes Verdict::Approve and exit_code returns 0. This leaves the original false-green failure mode intact for automation: `redteam review --base <base>` on a branch with no reviewable diff now says the verdict reflects zero reviewed content, but CI and callers that consume the verdict/exit code still receive a successful approve despite no cells having been reviewed.
recommendation: Treat zero reviewable cells as an incomplete review, not an approve: set `report.verdict = Verdict::Incomplete` and return exit code 2, or fail before fanout with a structured incomplete result. The warning can remain, but it must not be the only signal because machine consumers rely on verdict and exit status.

title: Contract-violating upheld findings are silently accepted
quote:
} else if lower.starts_with("upheld") || lower.starts_with("claim upheld") {
        (VerifyVerdict::Upheld, title.to_string(), None)
body: The refute prompt contract says an upheld claim must be represented only by an empty findings array and explicitly forbids titles like "Claim upheld …". This classifier nevertheless treats a non-empty finding starting with "upheld" or "claim upheld" as a clean Upheld result with no warning. That masks provider/template drift exactly where the verify layer depends on a machine-readable contract: a model can regress to emitting agreement findings forever and the run will show no warning, so operators cannot tell that refute outputs no longer obey the prompt. It also makes the parser depend on ambiguous natural-language titles instead of the documented empty-array signal.
recommendation: Make the parser match the prompt contract: only an empty findings array should produce Upheld without warning, and only an exact canonical "REFUTED: " machine prefix should produce Refuted. Treat any non-empty non-canonical output, including "upheld" / "Claim upheld" findings, as contract drift with a warning (preferably conservatively Upheld/unavailable rather than silently accepted).

title: Doc refute prompt requires line numbers it never provides
quote: - If you find concrete, grounded reasons the claim is WRONG / a false positive / actually addressed: return EXACTLY ONE finding — title = "REFUTED: " followed by the refutation reason, body = the evidence. The "REFUTED: " title prefix is the machine-read verdict signal (keep the prefix itself in English even when writing in another language). ALL schema fields are REQUIRED for the JSON to parse: fill severity, file, line_start, line_end by copying them from the claimed finding above; confidence = your certainty (0..1) that the claim is wrong; recommendation = one line on how to disposition the claim; quote may be empty.
body: The doc-refute template tells the verifier that `line_start` and `line_end` are required and must be copied from the claimed finding, but the `<claimed_finding>` block for document claims only includes `Document`, `Title`, `Severity`, `Body`, and `Claimed evidence`; it never renders `{{LINE_START}}` or `{{LINE_END}}`. A model following this contract has no source for two required schema fields, so it must either fabricate them or omit them. Omission makes the response fail `RawFinding` deserialization, turning a valid refutation into `refute unavailable`/upheld; fabrication corrupts the verification record. This is especially damaging for doc omissions, where refute is the safety net for false-positive omission findings.
recommendation: Render the claimed line range in the doc template, e.g. add `Location: {{FILE}}:{{LINE_START}}-{{LINE_END}}` or explicit `Line start`/`Line end` fields before requiring the verifier to copy them.

title: secrets.toml shape change silently discards all existing keys, and the first write_secret destroys the old file (irreversible)
quote: toml::from_str(&text).unwrap_or_default()
body: load_secrets() now deserializes into BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, SecretEntry>> but keeps the pre-existing `toml::from_str(&text).unwrap_or_default()`. Every pre-upgrade secrets.toml has the old flat shape `[provider] api_key = "sk-…"` (or `provider = "sk-…"`), which fails to deserialize into the nested map; unwrap_or_default() swallows the error and returns an empty map with no warning. Consequences: (1) resolve_key() falls through to secrets lookup only, finds nothing, and build_registry does `cfg.resolve_key(&pm.name).unwrap_or_default()` — every review runs with an empty API key and fails auth, with zero diagnostics pointing at secrets migration (contrast: config.toml legacy shapes get a hard bail with migration guidance; secrets get nothing). (2) Any parse error in the new shape is also silently swallowed to "no keys". (3) Data loss: the first `model setup --key-store secrets` after upgrade calls write_secret → load_secrets() (empty) → map gets only the new entry → `std::fs::write(&path, text)` overwrites the entire file, permanently destroying all previously stored keys with no backup. This is a hard, silent break of the upgrade path for every user who stored keys in secrets.toml.
recommendation: Make load_secrets() the single canonicalization point: distinguish file-missing from parse-failure; on parse failure, detect the legacy flat shape ({provider: string}) and hard-error with migration instructions (mirror the [providers.*] legacy-field bail in config/mod.rs) instead of returning an empty map. In write_secret, refuse to rewrite the file when the existing content failed to parse as the new shape (never destroy unreadable secret material); provide an explicit migration command that rewrites [X] key → [X."<model-id>"] once the model id is known.

title: `model setup --priority` is silently dropped — write_model takes no priority and never writes it; `let prio` is dead code
quote: let prio = priority.unwrap_or(0);
body: ModelCmd::Setup still accepts `--priority` (help text: "候补链优先级（大者先选）") and computes `let prio = priority.unwrap_or(0);`, but the new write_model signature has no priority parameter and the call site never passes it — `prio` is unused (a compiler dead-code warning the change ships anyway). The written `[models.X]` therefore never contains `priority`, so every CLI-configured model defaults to priority 0. Impact: resolve_models' candidate-chain ordering (all_by_priority sorts by model-level priority, falling back to BTreeMap name order on ties) silently degrades to alphabetical for all setup-created models; a user who deliberately sets `--priority 10` on their preferred model gets no error and no effect — silent configuration data loss. Related drift in the same command: `--context-tokens` help still says it writes `context_window_tokens`, and the stale `--help`/docstring field list in write_model still names the old provider fields.
recommendation: Add a priority parameter to write_model and persist it into `[models.X]` (Some → write explicit value, None → omit key), pass `prio` at the call site; or, if priority is being retired from setup, remove the flag entirely (clap error on use) instead of accepting-and-ignoring. Update the stale help/doc text for --priority and --context-tokens in the same change.

title: resolve_key() semantics changed from provider-keyed to model-keyed, but main.rs call sites still pass provider names — `model list --remote` loses the key for multi-model providers
quote: let key = cfg.resolve_key(&prov);
body: resolve_key(model) now starts with `self.models.get(model)?` and returns None for any name that is not a [models.*] key. Two main.rs sites were not updated: (1) `ModelCmd::List { remote }`: `let key = cfg.resolve_key(&prov);` where `prov` is a provider name. For a provider hosting multiple models (the exact 1:N case this change introduces), `models.get("agc")` is None → key=None → the /models probe is sent unauthenticated → false "error querying …/models" / 401 even though valid keys exist under [agc.glm-5.3]. If a model coincidentally shares the provider's name, only that one model's key is used. (2) `ModelCmd::Setup`'s post-write probe (`cfg.resolve_key(&provider)`) only works because write_model currently writes model_name == provider_name — it breaks the moment models under that provider use different names. This is a functional regression of the availability-check surface caused by the split.
recommendation: Route both probes through the model namespace: for `--remote`, resolve all cfg.models whose provider == prov, probe with effective_model/resolve_key per model (or require the model name shown by `model list`); for the setup probe, use the just-written model name explicitly. Alternatively give Config a provider-scoped key helper that iterates the provider's models, so "key for a channel" has one canonical resolution path.

title: write_model never updates an existing provider node — re-running `model setup` with a changed base_url/kind silently persists nothing and probes the old endpoint
body: The provider section is created with `providers_t.entry(provider_name).or_insert_with(|| { kind/base_url/api_key_env … })` — insert-if-absent only. Old write_provider replaced the whole `[providers.X]` table on every run, so re-running setup with a corrected `--base-url` (or different kind) updated the config. Now: the model node is rewritten, the provider node keeps its old values, validate_setup() blesses the NEW base_url, the success message prints, and the follow-up probe (load_config_warned → old base_url) tests the stale endpoint — the user's change is silently dropped with a green-looking output. Variants of the same overwrite asymmetry: `models_t.insert(model_name, …)` fully replaces the model table, so re-running setup for a second model under the same provider (model_name always == provider_name today) silently clobbers the first model's entry, and any hand-added keys on that model (priority, output_limit) are wiped on every setup run.
recommendation: On setup, upsert the provider node's kind/base_url/api_key_env to the values just validated (or diff-and-warn when they differ from what's on disk, refusing silent divergence). For the model node, merge-with-override of known keys instead of wholesale table replacement so manual model-level knobs survive re-setup; when model_name collides with an existing different model id, warn or require an explicit model name.

title: Legacy-shape detection is asymmetric: [models.*] silently ignores old field names (context_window_tokens, model) — silent 2.4x pack-budget shrink
quote: "model", "context_window_tokens", "priority", "per_turn_timeout_secs", "output_limit",
body: The migration guard added in from_layers_tagged hard-bails only for legacy fields inside `[providers.*]` ("不静默丢配置"). But the same users migrating by hand will naturally write the old field names under the new table — `[models.X] context_window_tokens = 1000000` or `model = "…"` — and ModelConfig has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so serde silently drops them. Result: context_window silently reads as None → effective_model/pack_budget_bytes fall back to the conservative 128K → budget drops from 768K to 312K (the exact cliff the tests document) with zero warning, and the declared 1M-window model is never honored. The change's own stated principle (never silently drop config on shape upgrade) is enforced on one side of the split and absent on the other.
recommendation: Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to ModelConfig (and ProviderConfig) so unknown/legacy keys hard-fail at the single deserialization point — this closes the class for all future renames too; or extend the legacy detection loop to scan the merged `models` table for `model`/`context_window_tokens` and emit the same directional migration error.

title: Exit code change for Incomplete verdict (from 2 to 3) and command errors (from 2 to 1) breaks automation compatibility
body: The five-tier exit code scheme (0=approve, 1=command error, 2=degraded approve, 3=incomplete, 10=reject) repurposed exit code 2 from its historical meaning of 'partial/incomplete' to 'degraded approve'. This silently shifts every code path that previously returned 2 for Incomplete (e.g., `partial_report`, `run_job` timeout/failure, `resolve_result` for non-terminal jobs) to exit 3, and every code path that returned 2 for command failures (e.g., bad args, bad config) to exit 1. Any CI/deployment script that checked for exit code 2 as 'not fully approved' will now see either 1 (error) or 3 (incomplete) and may misinterpret the result — most dangerously, treating exit 0 as the only failure case and proceeding with a degraded-approve report. The provided spec docs (SKILL.md, ship.md) do not define the exit codes, so this is not a spec violation, but the change is user-visible and breaks existing contracts without migration guidance. Affected call sites: `main.rs` lines using `std::process::exit(2)` changed to `exit(1)` (e.g., args parsing errors, job not found, bad config) and `cli/tail.rs` `exit_code(Verdict::Incomplete, _)` returning 3 instead of 2. `partial_report` (cli/mod.rs) and all three `run_job` outcome branches use the new 3. `resolve_result` in main.rs returns 1 for non-terminal jobs instead of 2.
recommendation: Document the exit codes in the `--help` output and in ship.md/SKILL.md. Consider adding a transition period where Incomplete still returns 2 if no explicit `--exit-format` is provided, or add a `--exit-codes` flag to opt into the new scheme. At minimum, ensure the changelog highlights the mapping change.

title: `resolve show` output appends human-readable history lines to pretty-printed JSON, breaking machine consumption
body:
The `resolve show` command (used by ship.md for cross-round state reconstruction) outputs a JSON block via `serde_json::to_string_pretty` and then appends `
history:
  (round)  reason...` as raw text lines. The resulting output is not valid JSON and cannot be parsed by jq or similar tools. The symmetrical `dismiss show` command outputs pure valid JSON (no appended lines), creating an inconsistency. Scripts that automate `resolve show <id>` to retrieve card details will misparse or fail. The ship.md protocol references `resolve show <id>` as a cross-round state reconstruction read, but does not specify whether the output must be machine-readable JSON or human-readable text — the current hybrid form satisfies neither.
recommendation: Either output pure JSON (including history as a JSON array field inside the card object) and let the client format it for display, or add a `--format` flag to `resolve show` to select between text/human and JSON output. Align with `dismiss show` behavior: prefer a unified `--format json|table` interface.

title: Fuzzy carry matching can silently erase a distinct new finding
quote:
c.id == n.id
                || (c.origin == Origin::Carried && crate::consolidate::dedup::is_same_bug(c, &n))
body: The new fallback treats any overlapping finding with a sufficiently similar title or quote as the same bug as a carried finding, even when their stable IDs differ. Two distinct defects can legitimately share a line range and a generic title such as "missing validation". In that case the new finding is discarded; only its model name is merged, while its ID, body, severity, confidence, recommendation, and `Origin::New` are lost. This is especially dangerous when the carried ID is dismissed: the merged result is subsequently marked dismissed under the old ID, so a genuinely new blocking defect can be exempted and the review can incorrectly approve. `stats.new` also no longer records it. Preserve ambiguous new findings instead of collapsing them based on this heuristic.
recommendation: Use exact ID matching for destructive carry absorption. If quote drift must be reconciled, retain both findings or emit an explicit ambiguous/re-anchored relationship for later adjudication; do not discard the new finding or inherit the carried finding's dismissal state unless identity is established deterministically.

title: A failed Pending-to-Running database update is converted into a successful worker exit
body: The initial state transition collapses every `JobStore::update_if_active` error into `false`. The following fallback reads an optional exit code and defaults to `0`; because read errors are also represented as no state, a database failure can make the worker exit successfully while the job remains Pending or Running. This is observably different from a legitimate terminal-freeze rejection and can leave automation believing the worker succeeded even though no review ran and no terminal state was recorded.
recommendation: Match all three outcomes explicitly: continue on `Ok(true)`, re-read and return the existing terminal code on `Ok(false)`, and log plus return command-failure code 1 on `Err(e)`. Do not default a missing or unreadable terminal exit code to success.

title: Worker spawn failure leaves an unreapable Pending job
body: The background path creates the job before spawning the detached worker, but the spawn-error branch exits without updating that job. The resulting state is Pending with no PID. `reap_if_dead` explicitly leaves Pending jobs without a PID untouched because it cannot determine liveness, so this record remains Pending indefinitely and can be mistaken for work that may still start. Repeated dispatch failures accumulate permanent zombie jobs.
recommendation: On spawn failure, use the already-open `JobStore` to transition the created job to `Failed`, recording the spawn error and exit code 1, before returning. If that terminal write also fails, surface both errors. Alternatively, make job creation and successful worker registration transactional through a launch state that can be deterministically reaped.

title: Partial and failed reports lack models/lenses metadata despite on_meta writing them to job state
quote:
run: RunMeta {
            job_id: job_id.to_string(),
            models: vec![],
            model_ids: vec![],
            lenses: vec![],
            duration_ms: 0,
            usage: Usage::default(),
            warnings: vec![format!("partial: {done}/{total} cells"), reason],
body:
When a job fails (Outcome::Done(Err)) or times out (Outcome::TimedOut), `partial_report` at ~line 573 constructs a `ReviewReport` with `RunMeta { models: vec![], lenses: vec![], ... }` — the models and lenses are left empty. This contradicts the purpose of the new `on_meta` hook, which writes models/lenses into the job state *before* the fan-out. A consumer polling for intermediate JSON (partial result after failure) will see empty `run.models` and `run.lenses`, even though those values were already persisted in the job state file. This creates an observability gap: downstream tooling cannot determine which models/lenses were configured for the incomplete job, defeating the incident‑response use case for which `on_meta` was added (r1 20260703).

The `partial_report` function should read `st.models` and `st.lenses` from the job state (or from the args) and populate them in the partial `RunMeta`.
recommendation: In `partial_report`, read the job state (via `read_state(ws, job_id)`) and propagate `st.models` and `st.lenses` into the partial `RunMeta` instead of unconditionally using empty vecs. This ensures that partial/failure reports carry the same metadata that `on_meta` already wrote.

title: The PID identity anchor is disabled on every platform except macOS
body: On Linux and all other non-macOS targets, newly spawned jobs always persist `pid_start=None`, so `is_worker_alive` degrades to `kill(pid, 0)` and cannot distinguish a reused PID from the original worker. A later `cancel` can therefore send SIGTERM to an unrelated process whose PID has been recycled, directly defeating the stated identity-anchor safety boundary. The tests are also unconditionally compiled: on these targets `start_time_self_is_stable` always fails, and `alive_self_reused_anchor_is_dead` constructs `None` and then incorrectly expects the liveness-only path to report dead.
recommendation: Implement a real identity anchor on every supported Unix target before using PIDs for signaling—for example Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time combined with boot identity, or preferably a retained pidfd/process handle that can be signaled without a PID-reuse race. Gate platform-specific tests only as a temporary CI measure; merely gating tests does not fix the unsafe cancellation behavior.

title: The parent still performs an unguarded stale write that can regress Running or overwrite a terminal state
quote:
st.pid_start = redteam::procinfo::start_time(pid);
                        let _ = redteam::state::job::write_state(&ws, &st);
body: After spawning the detached worker, the parent mutates its pre-spawn `st` snapshot and writes the entire state with `write_state`. The child can concurrently enter `run_job` and atomically advance the database to Running—or, for a fast/failing job, even to a terminal state—before this parent write occurs. The stale parent write then restores Pending and can overwrite Done/Failed/Cancelled, bypassing the new first-terminal freeze entirely. If the worker subsequently dies, the job may remain Pending indefinitely because lazy reaping only handles Running jobs. Adding the potentially blocking `start_time(pid)` lookup widens this existing interleaving window.
recommendation: Persist the PID and identity anchor through a guarded transactional update rather than `write_state`. The transaction must reject terminal states and should enforce the expected transition/snapshot, such as `Pending` with no conflicting worker identity. Ideally atomically claim the job for the spawned PID before the child is allowed to run, using a startup handshake so the parent PID write and child Pending-to-Running transition cannot reorder.

title: The global panic hook terminally fails the job for recoverable or unrelated panics
body: Rust panic hooks run when a panic begins, including panics that are subsequently caught with `catch_unwind` and panics in auxiliary runtime/provider tasks. This process-global hook therefore marks the job Failed before it is known that the top-level review is actually aborting. Because the guarded state machine freezes the first terminal state, a recoverable panic followed by successful review completion cannot write Done, leaving a valid result paired with an irreversible Failed status. Any unrelated panic on another worker thread has the same effect.
recommendation: Do not commit a terminal state from the process-global panic hook. Wrap the top-level worker future with an unwind boundary (for example `AssertUnwindSafe(...).catch_unwind()`) and call `mark_failed_panic` only when the panic escapes that top-level boundary. Keep the hook limited to diagnostics/default-hook delegation, and ensure spawned-task failures are handled according to orchestration semantics rather than globally freezing the job.

title: Lazy reaping ignores dead workers that never reached Running
body: The reaper immediately returns for Pending jobs, even though Pending is cancellable and the parent records a worker PID while the state is still Pending. A child can be killed, crash, or fail during startup before `run_job` commits Running; the persisted job then has a dead PID but remains Pending forever. This is especially reachable through the parent/child ordering race where the parent's stale PID write restores Pending after the child had already entered Running. Status/list will never repair such jobs, so the new lazy-reaping mechanism still leaves permanent nonterminal states.
recommendation: Reap both Pending and Running states when a PID is present and its anchored identity is definitively dead. To avoid falsely reaping the short spawn-registration window, atomically register/claim the worker identity before exposing the job, or introduce an explicit startup state/handshake and only reap Pending after registration is complete (optionally with a bounded startup grace period).

title: 配置 options 中 tools='off' 行为未定义
quote: config [review] tools = "off" | "two-stage"(默认候选) | "on"
body: §2.4 配置面定义 `[review] tools = "off" | "two-stage"(默认候选) | "on"`，但文档全篇未描述 tools='off' 的含义。off 是否完全禁用工具且无二阶段？是否保留 refute？off 与 two-stage 的区别是什么？该缺失导致实现者必须猜测，可能产生与设计不符的行为。此外，默认候选语义模糊（候选而不是决定），增加了不确定性。
recommendation: 明确 tools='off' 的行为语义，并确定默认值（移除‘候选’歧义）。如果 off 是无工具且无二阶段，需说明与 two-stage 的各自适用场景。

title: 验证成功标准含糊，仅凭一次 smoke 跑不足以保证 readiness
quote: 前置进批 1 验收的最低配：异语料 smoke 一跑。
body: §4 规定前置进批1验收的最低配为「异语料 smoke 一跑」，但未定义通过条件（例如：总轮次、质量分、错误率等）。后续回归监控项目也未设定阈值。没有明确的成功标准，无法客观判断默认翻转是否『ready』，评审者和实现者只能凭主观感受验收。
recommendation: 为 smoke 跑和回归监控项分别定义可量化的通过标准（例如：与原tools=on基线相比质量下降<5%，且轮次减少>80%等）。
